source_notes.label: Crystallite, particle and accessible surface are different quantities
source_notes.summary: The authors associate low BET area in low-water mixtures with sulfate-associated aggregation. Run3 has2.7nm Scherrer crystallites but about10nm TEM particles/aggregates; the reported particle-to-crystallite size ratio is3.7. This does not make the crystallites individually10nm. Runs4–7 surface-area estimates are described as comparable to crystallite size, suggesting single crystals; that is an interpretation, not atomic structural evidence.
source_locators: Supplied main pp.2–3, BET and TEM discussion

source_notes.label: Water, alcohol and reflux time affect the reported outcomes
source_notes.summary: The authors propose that water and higher reflux temperatures favor hydrolysis, while adsorbed alcohol obstructs it. The table retains all individual outcomes, including the nonmonotonic low-water sizes. No unreported mixture boiling temperatures or continuous size predictor are supplied.
source_locators: Supplied main p.2, hydrolysis and solvent discussion

source_notes.label: Surface cleaning depends on the treatment
source_notes.summary: Ammonia washing is associated with sulfate removal and higher surface area. Heating the ammonia-washed product at400°C for1h removes adsorbed ammonia; heating at600°C is associated with sulfate combustion and larger crystallites. The source does not establish that600°C material followed the ammonia/400°C sequence.
